title: ENARA Experiment 5 - pre-registration (current ENARA vs ENARA with language engine v2 vs plain AI tutor)
note: AI-simulated students only; not evidence about real learners. Locked before any run. This experiment tests the owner's ship bar: ENARA must clearly beat the plain AI tutor.
design: Same matched-triplet design as Experiment 4: each unit (student, outcome, replication) under A, B, C with identical hidden learner state and seeded behaviour flags; 50 new students (new seed) x 6 areas x 1 replication = 300 triplets on the 16 hold-out outcomes; 4 items per stage; 3 answer samples per item (majority); deterministic scoring; blind judge sample.

conditions.A: current ENARA, all v2 switches off
conditions.B: ENARA with ENARA_ENGINE_V2=all (wrongAnswer, belief, memory, cache)
conditions.C: plain AI tutor (same prompt and model as Experiments 3-4)

holdout.disclosure: The 16 hold-out outcomes were already scored under A, B (research flag) and C in Experiment 4, so aggregate results on them were seen; their transcripts were not read. The v2 changes were designed from code review plus Experiment 2-4 aggregate and transcript evidence on development outcomes. New students and a new seed are used, so no Experiment 4 block is reused.

primaryOutcome: Learning gain (post minus pre proportion correct on independent deterministic assessments).
secondaryOutcomes: input tokens and cache-read tokens per tutor call
sampleSize: 300 triplets, from the Experiment 4 variance of the per-triplet gain difference (0.152 for B-A; rule max(150, ceil(1.2*9.505*sigma2/0.08^2)) = 272, rounded up to 300). No pilot.
inference: Two-way (student x outcome) cluster bootstrap 95% CI; sign-flip permutation test on per-student mean differences; Holm-Bonferroni over the two confirmatory contrasts; Benjamini-Hochberg for exploratory contrasts; paired d_z with Hedges correction.
shipBar: The owner's bar: ENARA (B) clearly beats the plain tutor (C) = the B-C gain difference is positive with Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and a 95% CI that excludes 0. If not met, v2 is not shipped as a learning improvement. The cache feature is judged separately on measured cost.
decisionRules: B better than C (or A) only if Holm-adjusted p < 0.05 and the CI excludes 0. Failed or incomplete blocks stay in the data; unfavourable results are reported in full.
knownLimits: Single-session simulation: the memory feature (cross-session beliefs, spaced review, opening review) cannot show an effect because each simulated block is a fresh learner record; only wrongAnswer, belief and cache can act here. Simulated learners only; closing turn coincidence is not part of v2.
